---
title: "R bytecode compiler written in C"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    df_print: kable
params:
  ## One or more CSV files of crbcc_bench.py --csv, separated by commas. The
  ## files must have the suite install with gnur and crbcc, and the suite
  ## check, for example check.csv and results.csv of the CI. The gnur and
  ## crbcc results must come from the same machine, because the report
  ## divides their times.
  csv: "results.csv"
  ## If this value is not empty, the report writes two files for the crbcc
  ## README to this directory: the figure closures-time-by-size.png and the
  ## shields.io badge speedup.json.
  assets: ""
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, dev = "png", dpi = 120)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

## The categorical slots 1-2 of the dataviz reference palette, in a fixed order.
COL   <- c(gnur = "#2a78d6", crbcc = "#eb6834")
INK   <- "#0b0b0b"  # primary text
INK2  <- "#52514e"  # secondary text, axes
GRID  <- "#e4e3df"  # grid lines
RANGE <- "#c3c2b7"  # line between the compilers in a dot plot
COMPILERS <- names(COL)

## This list is the same as in crbcc_bench.py.
RECOMMENDED <- c("MASS", "lattice", "Matrix", "nlme", "survival", "boot",
                 "class", "cluster", "codetools", "foreign", "KernSmooth",
                 "mgcv", "nnet", "rpart", "spatial")

fmt   <- function(x, digits = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
pct   <- function(x) paste0(fmt(100 * x, 0), "%")
times <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(fmt(x, digits), "x")
gmean <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]; exp(mean(log(x))) }

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(
  text = element_text(colour = INK2),
  axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2),
  axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK),
  legend.text = element_text(colour = INK),
  strip.text = element_text(colour = INK, hjust = 0, size = 11),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = INK2),
  legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", legend.title = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)))
compiler_fill   <- scale_fill_manual(values = COL, breaks = COMPILERS)
compiler_colour <- scale_colour_manual(values = COL, breaks = COMPILERS)
log_x <- function(...) scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma(), ...)
log_y <- function(...) scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma(), ...)

# Read the CSV files -------------------------------------------------------

files <- trimws(strsplit(params$csv, ",")[[1]])
lines <- setNames(lapply(files, readLines), basename(files))
all <- bind_rows(lapply(names(lines), function(f)
  read.csv(text = grep("^#", lines[[f]], value = TRUE, invert = TRUE),
           colClasses = "character") |> mutate(source = f))) |>
  mutate(run = as.integer(run), value = as.numeric(value), size = as.numeric(size))

failed <- all |> filter(failure != "") |> distinct(suite, benchmark, compiler, run, failure)
## The suite install without the failed runs.
d <- all |> filter(suite == "install", failure == "")
## The suite check: the check result and the size of each crbcc closure. The
## failed runs stay, because they have the closures with a different byte code.
chk <- all |> filter(suite == "check", metric == "time")
if (!all(COMPILERS %in% d$compiler) || nrow(chk) == 0)
  stop("The CSV files must have the suite install with gnur and crbcc, and the suite check.")

runs <- tapply(d$run, d$compiler, n_distinct)
src  <- tapply(d$source, d$compiler, function(x) x[1])
## The check result of each closure. If more than one R process of an
## installation compiles a closure, the closure has more than one result.
checks <- chk |>
  group_by(benchmark, fn) |>
  summarise(check = if (any(check == "differs")) "differs"
                    else if (any(check == "same")) "same" else "unknown",
            .groups = "drop")
n_check <- table(factor(checks$check, c("same", "differs", "unknown")))

# Packages -----------------------------------------------------------------

## One row for each package, with the median of the runs for each metric and
## compiler, for example elapsed_gnur. A run can write more than one sample of
## a metric, one for each R process of R CMD INSTALL. Then the value of the
## run is the sum of its samples. A package without closures has no bytecode
## value, thus its bytecode time is 0. The longest
## elapsed_gnur is first.
pk <- d |>
  filter(metric %in% c("elapsed", "bytecode"), !is.na(value)) |>
  group_by(package = benchmark, compiler, metric, run) |>
  summarise(value = sum(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(package, compiler, metric) |>
  summarise(value = median(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(metric, compiler), values_from = value, values_fill = 0) |>
  ## Only the packages with results of the two compilers. For example, a
  ## package has no crbcc results if all its crbcc runs fail.
  filter(elapsed_gnur > 0, elapsed_crbcc > 0) |>
  mutate(group = if_else(package %in% RECOMMENDED, "recommended", "CRAN"), .after = package) |>
  arrange(desc(elapsed_gnur))
el <- c(gnur = sum(pk$elapsed_gnur), crbcc = sum(pk$elapsed_crbcc))
bc <- c(gnur = sum(pk$bytecode_gnur), crbcc = sum(pk$bytecode_crbcc))

# Closures -----------------------------------------------------------------

## One row for each closure: the median compile time of each compiler, the
## size in AST nodes, and the size class (powers of 10).
closures <- d |>
  filter(metric == "time") |>
  group_by(package = benchmark, fn, compiler) |>
  summarise(time = median(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = compiler, values_from = time) |>
  inner_join(chk |> filter(!is.na(size)) |> distinct(package = benchmark, fn, size),
             by = c("package", "fn")) |>
  filter(!is.na(gnur), !is.na(crbcc)) |>
  mutate(class = cut(size, c(1, 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, Inf),
                     c("1-9", "10-99", "100-999", "1,000-9,999", ">= 10,000"), right = FALSE))

# Badge for the README -----------------------------------------------------

if (nzchar(params$assets)) {
  dir.create(params$assets, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  writeLines(sprintf('{"schemaVersion": 1, "label": "compile speedup", "message": "%s faster than GNU R", "color": "blue"}',
                     times(bc[["gnur"]] / bc[["crbcc"]])),
             file.path(params$assets, "speedup.json"))
}
```

crbcc compiles R code to byte code. It gives the same byte code as the
compiler package of GNU R, but it is faster.

- [README and source code](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/crbcc#readme)
- [Use crbcc](https://prl-prg.github.io/crbcc/crbcc.html): compile closures
  and install packages with crbcc
- [crbcc on CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=crbcc)

<!-- end of the list -->

- **Installation:** with crbcc, `R CMD INSTALL` of `r nrow(pk)` packages
  takes `r fmt(el[["crbcc"]])` s, not `r fmt(el[["gnur"]])` s with GNU R
  (`r pct(1 - el[["crbcc"]] / el[["gnur"]])` less).
- **Byte-code compilation:** crbcc compiles the closures of these packages
  `r times(bc[["gnur"]] / bc[["crbcc"]])` faster than GNU R
  (`r fmt(bc[["crbcc"]], 2)` s, not `r fmt(bc[["gnur"]])` s).
- **Correctness:** the byte code of `r fmt(n_check[["same"]], 0)` of
  `r fmt(n_check[["same"]] + n_check[["differs"]], 0)` closures is the same
  as the GNU R byte code.

## Methodology

Each benchmark installs one package with `R CMD INSTALL`. The hook
`inst/r-cmd-install-hook.R` (`R_PROFILE_USER`) replaces
`compiler:::tryCmpfun`, which R uses to compile each closure of the package.
The replacement compiles the closure with GNU R (`gnur`, `compiler::cmpfun`)
or with crbcc (`crbcc`, `crbcc::cmpfun`) and measures the compile time.

- **elapsed**: the wall time of `R CMD INSTALL`.
- **bytecode**: the time in the byte-code compiler, for all closures that R
  compiles during the installation. These closures include the S4 methods.
- **compile time of a closure**: the time of one compilation, during the
  installation.
- **correctness**: the suite `check` installs each package of the Docker
  image one time with crbcc. The hook compares the byte code of each closure with the GNU R
  byte code in the Docker image (`identical()` with all strict flags). A run
  with a different byte code is a failure. The runs that measure the time do
  not compare, because the comparison adds time to the installation.

In the benchmark Docker image, the package tarballs have the compiled
native code of a previous installation. `R CMD INSTALL
--no-configure` does not compile this code again. Thus the elapsed time is
the time of the R part of the installation. The size of a closure is the
number of AST nodes of its body and of the default values of its formals
(`crbcc:::function_size`), from the suite `check`. The speedup of a group
of closures is the geometric mean of the speedups of the closures.

- Packages: `r nrow(pk)` (`r sum(pk$group == "recommended")` recommended,
  `r sum(pk$group == "CRAN")` CRAN).
- `gnur`: `r runs[["gnur"]]` runs of each package, from `r src[["gnur"]]`.
- `crbcc`: `r runs[["crbcc"]]` runs of each package, from `r src[["crbcc"]]`.

The section [Environment](#environment) gives the machine of each file. The
tables and figures show the median of the runs.

## Results

### Correctness

Of `r fmt(sum(n_check), 0)` closures, `r fmt(n_check[["same"]], 0)` have the
same byte code as GNU R, and `r fmt(n_check[["differs"]], 0)` have a
different byte code. For `r fmt(n_check[["unknown"]], 0)` closures, the
baseline has no byte code, for example for a closure that the JIT compiles in
a different R process.

```{r differs, eval = n_check[["differs"]] > 0}
checks |> filter(check == "differs") |> count(package = benchmark, name = "closures") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Closures with a different byte code")
```

```{r failed, eval = nrow(failed) > 0}
knitr::kable(failed, caption = "Runs with a failure. The results do not include these runs.")
```

### Installation time

```{r install-summary}
tibble(compiler = COMPILERS,
       `elapsed (s)` = fmt(el, 1),
       `bytecode (s)` = fmt(bc, 2),
       `bytecode share` = pct(bc / el))
```

The bytecode share is the part of the installation time in the byte-code
compiler. In the other time, R parses the code, makes the lazy-load database
and the help pages, and loads the package to test it.

```{r install-time-plot, fig.height = 1.5 + 0.25 * nrow(pk)}
pk |>
  pivot_longer(-c(package, group), names_to = c("metric", "compiler"), names_sep = "_") |>
  mutate(package = factor(package, rev(pk$package)),
         metric = factor(metric, c("elapsed", "bytecode"),
                         c("elapsed time of R CMD INSTALL (s)", "byte-code compile time (s)"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, package)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = package), colour = RANGE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = compiler), shape = 21, colour = "white", size = 3.2, stroke = 0.8) +
  compiler_fill + log_x() + labs(x = "s (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x")
```

The table has one row for each package. The largest byte-code speedup is
first.

- **gnur (s)**, **crbcc (s)**: the elapsed time of `R CMD INSTALL` with each
  compiler.
- **gnur / crbcc**: the installation speedup.
- **bytecode gnur (s)**, **bytecode crbcc (s)**: the time in the byte-code
  compiler.
- **bytecode gnur / crbcc**: the byte-code compilation speedup. If R
  compiles no closure of a package, the two bytecode times are 0. Then the
  speedup is not a number (`NaNx`), and the package is last.
- **bytecode share gnur**: bytecode gnur (s) divided by gnur (s), the part
  of the GNU R installation time in the byte-code compiler. This is
  approximately the maximum part of the installation time that crbcc can
  save.

```{r install-time-table}
pk |>
  arrange(desc(bytecode_gnur / bytecode_crbcc)) |>
  transmute(package, group,
            `gnur (s)` = fmt(elapsed_gnur, 2),
            `crbcc (s)` = fmt(elapsed_crbcc, 2),
            `gnur / crbcc` = times(elapsed_gnur / elapsed_crbcc, 2),
            `bytecode gnur (s)` = fmt(bytecode_gnur, 2),
            `bytecode crbcc (s)` = fmt(bytecode_crbcc, 3),
            `bytecode gnur / crbcc` = times(bytecode_gnur / bytecode_crbcc),
            `bytecode share gnur` = pct(bytecode_gnur / elapsed_gnur))
```

### Function size

The compile time of each closure, by the size of the closure. There are
`r fmt(nrow(closures), 0)` closures. The median size is
`r fmt(median(closures$size), 0)` nodes, and the largest closure (in
`r closures$package[which.max(closures$size)]`) has
`r fmt(max(closures$size), 0)` nodes.

```{r fn-table}
closures |>
  group_by(`size (AST nodes)` = class) |>
  summarise(closures = fmt(n(), 0),
            `gnur (us)` = fmt(median(gnur) * 1e6),
            `crbcc (us)` = fmt(median(crbcc) * 1e6),
            `gnur / crbcc` = times(gmean(gnur / crbcc)))
```

```{r fn-time-plot, fig.height = 6}
long <- closures |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(COMPILERS), names_to = "compiler", values_to = "time") |>
  mutate(compiler = factor(compiler, COMPILERS))
mid <- long |>
  group_by(compiler, class) |>
  summarise(size = median(size), time = median(time), .groups = "drop")
p <- ggplot(long, aes(size, time * 1e6, colour = compiler)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.3, stroke = 0) +
  geom_line(data = mid, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = mid, aes(fill = compiler), shape = 21, colour = "white",
             size = 3, stroke = 0.8) +
  compiler_colour + compiler_fill + log_x() + log_y() +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
  labs(x = "closure size (AST nodes, log scale)", y = "compile time (us, log scale)",
       subtitle = "The points are closures. The line is the median of the size class.")
if (nzchar(params$assets))
  ggsave(file.path(params$assets, "closures-time-by-size.png"), p,
         width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 120, bg = "white")
p
```

```{r fn-speedup-plot, fig.height = 4.5}
x <- closures |> mutate(speedup = gnur / crbcc) |> filter(is.finite(speedup), speedup > 0)
mid <- x |>
  group_by(class) |>
  summarise(size = median(size), speedup = gmean(speedup), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(x, aes(size, speedup)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.35, stroke = 0, colour = COL[["crbcc"]]) +
  geom_line(data = mid, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = mid, colour = INK, size = 2.5) +
  log_x() + log_y() +
  labs(x = "closure size (AST nodes, log scale)", y = "speedup, gnur / crbcc (log scale)",
       subtitle = "The points are closures. The line is the geometric mean of the size class.")
```

#### By package

The column "gnur / crbcc total" is the sum of the closure times with `gnur`,
divided by the sum with `crbcc`.

```{r fn-package}
closures |>
  group_by(package) |>
  summarise(closures = fmt(n(), 0), `median size` = fmt(median(size), 0),
            largest = fmt(max(size), 0),
            `gnur / crbcc total` = times(sum(gnur) / sum(crbcc)),
            `gnur / crbcc geo. mean` = times(gmean(gnur / crbcc))) |>
  arrange(match(package, pk$package))
```

#### Slowest closures

The 10 closures with the longest `crbcc` compile time:

```{r fn-slowest}
closures |> slice_max(crbcc, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  transmute(package, size = fmt(size, 0),
            `gnur (us)` = fmt(gnur * 1e6), `crbcc (us)` = fmt(crbcc * 1e6),
            `gnur / crbcc` = times(gnur / crbcc))
```

## Reproduce

### Input

The report reads the `--csv` reports of `inst/benchmarks/crbcc_bench.py`
(`params$csv`). The files must have the suite `install` with `gnur` and
`crbcc`, and the suite `check`. The docstring of `crbcc_bench.py` gives the
columns and the metrics. The `gnur` and `crbcc` results must come from the
same machine, because the report divides their times.

To make this report again in the Docker image, run these commands in a work
directory that has the crbcc source in `crbcc/`:

    mkdir -p pkg-lib
    R CMD INSTALL --library=pkg-lib crbcc
    crbcc/inst/benchmarks/crbcc_bench.py --r "$(which R)" \
      --prebuilt /opt/crbcc-benchmarks \
      --packages top50 --packages recommended --csv results.csv
    Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("crbcc/inst/benchmarks/crbcc_bench.Rmd",
      output_dir = ".", knit_root_dir = getwd(),
      params = list(csv = "results.csv"))'

With `--prebuilt`, `crbcc_bench.py` runs the suites `check` and `install`.
For the options, use `--help`.

### Environment

```{r env}
bind_rows(lapply(names(lines), function(f) {
  meta <- sub("^# ", "", grep("^#", lines[[f]], value = TRUE))
  tibble(key = sub(": .*", "", meta), value = sub("^[^:]*: ", "", meta), file = f)
})) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = file, values_from = value, values_fill = "")
```
